hints: Hint 1: Look carefully at each row and ask yourself, does a prokaryote even have that structure? Remember prokaryotes have no membrane-bound organelles.
Hint 2: Think about how DNA is packaged in each cell, and remember the size rule: prokaryotic 70S ribosomes are smaller than eukaryotic 80S ribosomes.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Recall the typical prokaryote plan**
Think small and simple. A prokaryote has no true nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles like ER, mitochondria or chloroplasts.

It has circular, naked DNA free in the cytoplasm, plus small 70S ribosomes.

Step 2: **Recall the typical eukaryote plan**
Think larger and compartmentalised. A eukaryote has a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles including rough and smooth ER.

Its nuclear DNA is linear and wrapped around histone proteins to form chromosomes, plus larger 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm.

Step 3: **Test each comparison**
Option A fails on the word only, because eukaryotes also have small circular DNA in mitochondria and chloroplasts. Option C fails because prokaryotes have no ER at all. Option D has the ribosome sizes the wrong way round.

Only option B matches both sides perfectly: naked DNA in prokaryotes, DNA associated with histone protein in eukaryotes.

options.A: Prokaryotes do have circular DNA, but eukaryotes do not have linear DNA only because mitochondria and chloroplasts contain small circular DNA.
options.B: Correct. Prokaryotic DNA is naked and free in the cytoplasm, while eukaryotic nuclear DNA is linear and wound around histone proteins.
options.C: Prokaryotes have no endoplasmic reticulum at all, as they lack all membrane-bound organelles.
options.D: The sizes are reversed. Prokaryotic 70S ribosomes are smaller (about $20 \text{ nm}$) than eukaryotic 80S ribosomes (about $22$ to $25 \text{ nm}$).
